id: -65-龐培在伊比利亞與阿爾巴尼亞的戰役
theater: 高加索伊比利亞與阿爾巴尼亞

battle.name: 龐培在伊比利亞與阿爾巴尼亞的戰役
battle.theater: 高加索伊比利亞與阿爾巴尼亞
battle.brief: 公元前65年第三次米特拉達梯戰爭末段，龐培以羅馬東方總督身分率軍攻入黑海東岸的科爾基斯，迫米特里達梯六世的最後基地出降，再北向高加索伊比利亞與阿爾巴尼亞，逼兩國國王送出人質納貢。卡面的投石機即羅馬重型扭力弩砲，攻城用來砸壞城牆，野戰用來打散密集戰陣，是本役攻城拔寨的骨幹。

kit.name: 投石機
kit.history: 把絞盤的勢能換成一塊石頭。攻城從此有了可以計算的破壞力。

countries: 這一條戰役名稱中的「伊比利亞」與「阿爾巴尼亞」都不是今天的西班牙與南歐：伊比利亞指高加索黑海東岸的伊比利亞王國，國土在今喬治亞中部，國王為法爾納瓦茲二世（瓦爾札刻斯）一系；阿爾巴尼亞指里海西南岸的高加索阿爾巴尼亞王國，疆域沿庫拉河下游伸入今亞塞拜然境內。兩者都是公元前65年龐培高加索行動的對象。交戰一方是羅馬共和國：龐培憑元老院授予的東方總督權，接管比提尼亞、龐圖斯、西里西亞以及克拉蘇留下的東方行省，麾下是老兵軍團、行省輔助軍、克里米亞與高加索諸部落的徵召民兵，另設攻城器械隊，專管雲梯、撞槌與擲石器。另一方是一個鬆散的聯盟：蓬提庫斯王國的米特里達梯六世與他安插在科爾基斯的代理人，連同伊比利亞與高加索阿爾巴尼亞的國王、王子，以及控制山口的部落聯盟。羅馬一方並非單一常備軍，而是由授權、募兵、編制與戰俘改編拼成的軍事體系；被征服地區的附庸兵也編入軍隊，成為其作戰體系的一部分。
countriesEn: In the name of this war the Iberian and the Albanian are neither modern Spain nor southern Europe. Iberia here is the kingdom of Iberia on the eastern Black Sea coast of the Caucasus, whose territory lay in what is now central Georgia under a line of kings headed by Pharnavaz II (Varzaces); Albania here is the Caucasian kingdom of Albania on the south-western shore of the Caspian, its lands running down the lower Kura river into what is now Azerbaijan. Both were the objects of Pompey's Caucasian operations in 65 BC. One side of the conflict is the Roman Republic: holding the eastern proconsular authority granted him by the Senate, Pompey took over Bithynia, Pontus, Cilicia and the eastern provinces that Crassus had left behind; under him were veteran legions, provincial auxiliaries, and levies recruited among the Crimean and Caucasian peoples, with a separate siege train under engineers who handled scaling ladders, battering rams and stone-throwers. The other side is a loose coalition: Mithridates VI of Pontus with the agents he had installed in Colchis, together with the kings and princes of Iberia and Caucasian Albania, plus the tribal coalitions that held the mountain passes. The Roman side was not a single standing army but a military system assembled from mandates, recruitment, levy organisation and the reorganisation of prisoners of war; the client troops of conquered regions were likewise folded into the force and formed part of its fighting power.
people: 全場戰役的樞紐是格奈烏斯·龐培（龐培大帝）：公元前66至65年間他在政治上取得元老院信任，被派往東方收拾第三次米特拉達梯戰爭，先以總督身分接手盧庫路斯的戰區，再逐步把軍權、財權與戰利品分配權收攏到自己手上。前任盧庫路斯留下的是提格拉諾刻達與阿爾塔沙特兩場勝利，以及被劫掠一空的亞美尼亞國庫；龐培接手時，亞美尼亞的財富與黑海東岸米特里達梯的殘部都還在場上。龐培身邊有執政官級的副手，如阿夫拉尼烏斯、加比尼烏斯等人，負責分遣支軍、監督徵召與押送戰利品；加比尼烏斯後來還奉龐培之命出使埃及，這次東征是他外交生涯的起點。對面一方的主腦是米特里達梯六世：他不能容忍羅馬在東方建立的秩序，先在科爾基斯立自己的兒子馬卡雷斯為王，馬卡雷斯其後自殺，繼位者再被推翻；提格拉涅二世在亞美尼亞遭到米特里達梯反咬，國勢崩解；伊比利亞王國內部有王位繼承與亞美尼亞王位歸屬的爭端，阿爾斯托刻斯等人起兵；高加索阿爾巴尼亞的國王則在外交上左右逢源。史料作者普魯塔克與阿庇安留下的敘述，決定了今日我們能知道這場戰役的樣貌。
peopleEn: The pivot of the whole campaign is Gnaeus Pompeius Magnus, Pompey the Great. Between 66 and 65 BC he won the confidence of the Senate and was sent east to finish the Third Mithridatic War: he first took over Lucullus's theatre of operations as proconsul, and then gradually concentrated in his own hands the command, the financial control and the right to distribute the booty. His predecessor Lucullus left behind the victories of Tigranocerta and Artaxata and a thoroughly plundered Armenian treasury; when Pompey took over, the wealth of Armenia and the surviving followers of Mithridates on the eastern Black Sea coast were both still on the table. Around Pompey stood lieutenants of praetorian standing such as Afranius and Gabinius, who were responsible for detaching detachments, supervising recruitment and escorting the spoils; Gabinius would later be sent by Pompey to Egypt, and this eastern campaign was the beginning of his diplomatic career. On the other side the driving mind was Mithridates VI of Pontus, who could not tolerate the order Rome had established in the East: he first set his own son Machares on the throne in Colchis, Machares then killed himself, and his successor was overthrown in turn; Tigranes II of Armenia was bitten back by Mithridates and his kingdom fell apart; inside the Iberian kingdom there was a dispute over the succession and over the ownership of the Armenian crown, with men such as Artoces rising in revolt; and the king of Caucasian Albania hedged his bets in every direction. The narrative that survives, by the hands of Plutarch and Appian, is what fixes the shape of this war as we know it today.
kits: 卡面這件投石機，是羅馬重型扭力投射器的代表：把絞盤儲存的扭力轉成拋射一塊石頭或一束標槍的動能，機身低矮、底座沉重、必須靠畜力牽引，隨軍由受訓工匠操作。按羅馬圍城的常規做法，它屬攻城器械隊，與撞槌、覆蓋式攻城塔、斜坡掩體（vineae）以及大型弩砲（ballista）配套：圍城先以壕溝與圍牆斷絕城內補給，再把弩砲與擲石器布於陣地，用以壓制城頭火力、砸壞城垛與塔樓，逼守軍退入內城；石彈不足時，擲石器也用來拋射燃燒物或小型標槍。野戰時這類器械可用來打散密集的部落戰陣與守軍隊形，掩護步戰與騎兵接近。羅馬步兵裝備是分段式大盾（scutum）、投槍（pilum）與短劍，配鎖子甲或分段甲；輔助軍以弓手（克里特弓與弓兵）與投石索手為主，騎兵來自行省。糧秣與石彈依賴騾車隊與馱獸，龐培的遠征因山道狹窄、冬季降雪而屢屢延誤。對手方面，米特里達梯以工程技術與火攻著稱，蓬提庫斯的攻城器械一度令羅馬的攻堅蒙受損失，而黑海東岸兩座要塞裏儲存的巨大財富，則是這場戰役的實際繳獲。
kitsEn: The onager on the card is the representative piece of Roman heavy torsion artillery: it converts the torsion stored by a windlass into the momentum that hurls a stone or a bundle of javelins. The frame is low, the base heavy, the machine has to be towed by draught animals, and it is worked in the field by trained engineers. By the standard Roman practice of siege it belonged to the siege train and worked in company with battering rams, covered siege towers, the sloping protective galleries (vineae) and the heavy bolt-shooters (ballistae): a siege began by cutting the defenders off from food and water with a trench and a circumvallation, and only then were the bolt-shooters and stone-throwers deployed in the lines, to silence the fire from the walls, to smash battlements and towers and to drive the garrison back into the inner city; when stone ammunition ran short, the throwers could also lob burning material or light javelins. In the open field such engines could be used to break up dense tribal formations and close-order bodies of troops, covering the approach of the infantry and the cavalry. Roman infantry equipment was the segmented large shield (scutum), the throwing javelin (pilum) and the short sword, worn with mail or scale armour; the auxiliaries were mainly archers (Cretan and composite bowmen) and slingers, and the cavalry was drawn from the provinces. Food, fodder and stone ammunition depended on mule trains and pack animals, and Pompey's march was repeatedly delayed by narrow passes and winter snow. On the opposing side Mithridates was celebrated for engineering and for fire, and the siege works of Pontus at times cost the Romans dearly; the great wealth stored in the two fortresses of the eastern Black Sea coast was, in the end, the real prize of this campaign.
tactics: 羅馬軍在東方的作戰方式，是野戰與圍城兩套手法的組合。野戰靠軍團以雙重陣列展開：前排重裝步卒用大盾結成盾牆迎敵，中排待前排力竭換上，後排保留為預備；兩翼是行省弓手與投石索手，負責壓制敵方射手，騎兵在側翼尋找戰機，一有機會就衝擊敵陣側背。龐培在高加索面對的並非有備的正面大軍，而是熟悉山地的部落聯盟：這些部隊慣於在林地與峽谷中游擊，觸即即走，故羅軍的應對是結隊行軍、嚴設警戒、以先鋒騎兵搜索山道，再以縱隊深遠推進，切斷各部落之間的聯繫；史料提到雙方在河谷與山口的遭遇戰，多靠地形與突襲取勝。圍城時程序固定：先取一處制高點設營，挖壕、築柵、造圍牆，斷敵糧水；再以攻城塔與覆蓋通道逼近，用擲石器與弩砲持續轟擊城牆，最後才以撞槌和突擊步兵同時衝多處缺口。軍營本身是戰役的一部分，按羅馬規矩每日挖掘壕溝、設置望樓與照明警哨，後方有輜重隊與工匠營，糧草由騾車隊與海運補充。
tacticsEn: The way the Roman army fought in the East combined two sets of method, one for the open field and one for siege. In the field the legions deployed in a double battle line: the heavy infantry of the front rank met the enemy behind a wall of large shields, the second rank stepped in as the first grew tired, and the third was kept back as reserve; on both flanks provincial archers and slingers were posted to shoot down enemy skirmishers, while cavalry hunted for chances on the wings and struck at the flank or rear of the opposing line when one appeared. What Pompey faced in the Caucasus was not a prepared army in the open but a coalition of tribes at home in the mountains, troops accustomed to skirmishing in woodland and gorges and breaking off the moment they were pressed; the Roman answer was to march in column, to keep a strict watch, to have the cavalry screen the mountain roads, and to push deep in order to cut the tribes off from one another. The encounters fought in the river valleys and at the passes were, in the ancient account, won as much by the ground and by surprise as by the weight of the troops. The siege followed a fixed routine: first a camp was pitched on commanding ground, with ditch, rampart and palisade dug to cut the defenders off from food and water; then the siege towers and covered approaches were brought forward and the walls were hammered continuously by stone-throwers and bolt-shooters; only at the end did the rams and the assaulting infantry strike several breaches at once. The camp itself was part of the campaign: by Roman custom the trench was dug afresh each day, watchtowers and lighted sentry posts were set, and behind the lines came the baggage train and the engineers' camp, with grain supplied by mule teams and by sea.
data: 可核對的數字不多，且多為年代而非兵力。時間線是：第三次米特拉達梯戰爭自公元前74年打到公元前63年；盧庫路斯於公元前69年取提格拉諾刻達、前68年取阿爾塔沙特；元老院把東方戰爭的收尾權交給龐培在公元前66至65年；本役的高加索階段記於公元前65年；米特里達梯最遲在公元前63年被自己人刺殺，第三次米特拉達梯戰爭告終；龐培的凱旋式在公元前61年秋天舉行。地理尺度可以估算：里海（庫拉河）河道全長約一千三百六十公里，黑海東岸的科爾基斯海岸多雨，冬季山道常因積雪與泥濘封閉，羅馬軍隊若要從比提尼亞走到高加索腹地，靠的是冬春之間的短暫窗口，糧秣與飼料多靠海運至法西斯一帶再轉陸路。戰利品方面，古代記載形容龐培在科爾基斯所得極為可觀，並提到羅馬士兵因此得到大額分賞，但具體數目各家互相矛盾，不宜當作精確值。兵力數字在史料中幾乎空白：一般只能說羅馬遠征軍以數個老兵軍團為骨幹，輔以數量可觀的行省輔助軍與高加索徵召民兵，而真正的限制是糧食與飼料，不是戰鬥人數。重建此役還有一個麻煩：主要依據是普魯塔克《龐培傳》與阿庇安《米特拉達梯戰爭》的殘篇，兩書都偏重戲劇性與道德評判，地名、人名與事件次序都需要互相對照，因此本條目的細節只宜當作大框架看待。
dataEn: There are not many checkable figures, and most of them are dates rather than numbers of men. The chronology runs as follows: the Third Mithridatic War was fought from 74 to 63 BC; Lucullus took Tigranocerta in 69 BC and Artaxata in 68 BC; the Senate handed the finishing of the eastern war to Pompey in 66 to 65 BC; the Caucasian phase of this campaign is dated to 65 BC; Mithridates was killed by his own men at the latest in 63 BC, which ended the Third Mithridatic War; and Pompey celebrated his triumph in the autumn of 61 BC. Some scale can be given geographically: the Kura, which drains into the Caspian, runs about 1,360 kilometres in all, and the Colchian coast of the eastern Black Sea is wet, the mountain tracks being closed in winter by snow and mud. For a Roman army to move from Bithynia into the heart of the Caucasus depended on the short window between winter and spring, and grain and fodder came by sea as far as Phasis before being transferred to pack animals. On the spoils, the ancient writers describe what Pompey took in Colchis as enormous and note that his soldiers received large distributions, but the figures given contradict one another and should not be treated as exact. Numbers of troops are practically absent from the record: all that can be said is that the expedition was built on several veteran legions, supported by a substantial body of provincial auxiliaries and Caucasian levies, and that the binding constraint was food and fodder rather than man power. There is one further difficulty in reconstructing the campaign: the main bases are the surviving fragments of Plutarch's Life of Pompey and Appian's Mithridatic Wars, works that favour the dramatic and the moral, so place names, personal names and the order of events all have to be cross-checked. The detail given here should therefore be taken as an outline rather than a settled account.
cause: 要理解這場戰役，先要分清三層原因。第一層是米特里達梯的攻勢：公元前67年盧庫路斯奪走他的亞美尼亞，公元前65年米特里達梯反過來撲向亞美尼亞，擊敗提格拉涅之子，把羅馬在東方的附庸秩序攪亂，也令龐圖斯與比提尼亞的戰線直接受威。第二層是羅馬的戰略安排：米特里達梯退守黑海東岸的科爾基斯，仍握有黑海艦隊與大筆財富，若任他重建基地，形同在羅馬背後留了一把刀；元老院於是給龐培東方總督權，讓他一次性解決蓬提庫斯殘部。第三層是羅馬在高加索的利益：伊比利亞與高加索阿爾巴尼亞的國王早已遣使到羅馬送貢求庇護，羅馬也支持伊比利亞王族對亞美尼亞王位的繼承要求；這次行動要把這兩國正式置於羅馬的宗主地位之下，切斷他們與米特里達梯的往來，同時把羅馬的邊界推到黑海至里海一線，為東向的商路與情報站穩定後方。至於「龐培在伊比利亞與阿爾巴尼亞的戰役」這個名稱，正是指這一段高加索行動：維基百科的英文條目現已改掛在「龐培的高加索戰役」名下，內容正是公元前65年這一段。
causeEn: To understand this war one must first separate three layers of cause. The first is Mithridates' own offensive: in 67 BC Lucullus had taken his Armenia away from him, and in 65 BC Mithridates turned and struck at Armenia, defeating Tigranes' son, disrupting the client order Rome had established in the East and putting the Pontic and Bithynian fronts directly at risk. The second is Roman strategic calculation: Mithridates, driven back to Colchis on the eastern Black Sea, still held a fleet and great wealth, and if he were allowed to rebuild a base he would be a knife at Rome's back. The Senate therefore gave Pompey the eastern proconsular authority and let him settle the Pontus remnant in one stroke. The third is Rome's interest in the Caucasus itself: the kings of Iberia and of Caucasian Albania had already sent embassies to Rome with tribute and requests for protection, and Rome backed the Iberian royal house in its claim to the Armenian crown. This operation was meant to place both countries formally under Roman suzerainty, to cut their lines of communication with Mithridates, and at the same time to push the Roman frontier forward to the Black Sea and Caspian line, so as to steady the rear of the trade routes and listening posts that pointed east. The name itself, Pompey's campaign in Iberia and Albania, refers precisely to this Caucasian operation: the English Wikipedia article now sits under the title of the Caucasian campaign of Pompey, and its subject is exactly this episode of 65 BC.
impact: 短期的結果是高加索重新排列：科爾基斯被納入羅馬的勢力範圍，成為受羅馬監督、按期繳納貢賦的附庸；伊比利亞與高加索阿爾巴尼亞的國王接受人質與納貢條款，成為羅馬的附庸國；黑海東岸的航線與里海方向的中亞商路，開始落在羅馬的注視之下。這對後世有兩層意思。一是羅馬在東方的邊界從安納托利亞內陸推到黑海—里海一線，黑海東岸與高加索從此成為羅馬與帕提亞、其後薩珊波斯角力的前沿，喬治亞與亞塞拜然一帶的地緣格局此後數百年都受這條線牽動。二是羅馬在這裡沒有設行省，而是用附庸國、外交條款與少量駐軍維持控制，開創了羅馬處理高加索的長期模式；這個模式在往後的亞美尼亞戰爭、龐培與安息人的較量裡一再重演，而龐培自己在高加索掙來的權威，也直接推高了他返羅馬後的政治資本。公元前61年的凱旋式與隨後與凱撒、克拉蘇結成的同盟，最終把這批資本變成了公元前49年的內戰，羅馬共和國的裂痕，最初正是在這樣一片外戰收尾之後才全面爆開。
impactEn: In the short term the Caucasus was rearranged: Colchis was brought into the Roman sphere and became a client district under Roman supervision, paying tribute on schedule; the kings of Iberia and of Caucasian Albania accepted the terms of hostages and tribute and became Roman client kingdoms; and the shipping lanes of the eastern Black Sea, together with the Central Asian trade routes running toward the Caspian, came under Roman notice. For later ages this had two layers of meaning. First, Rome's eastern frontier moved from the interior of Anatolia forward to the Black Sea and Caspian line, and the eastern Black Sea coast and the Caucasus became the front where Rome would contest the Parthians and, after them, the Sasanian Persians; the geopolitics of the Georgian and Azerbaijani region would be shaped by that line for centuries. Second, Rome did not make provinces here. It held the Caucasus with client kingdoms, diplomatic clauses and a small garrison, and that became Rome's long-term way of dealing with the region. The pattern was repeated in the later wars over Armenia and in Pompey's dealings with the Parthians, and the authority Pompey won for himself in the Caucasus directly raised his political capital on his return to Rome. His triumph of 61 BC and the alliance he then concluded with Caesar and Crassus finally turned that capital into the civil war of 49 BC: the cracks in the Roman Republic first opened wide after an eastern war of this kind had been closed out.
result: 就戰役本身，結果是羅馬勝利：科爾基斯陷落，米特里達梯六世在高加索的最後基地被拔除，逃往博斯普魯斯的繼位者被部下所殺；伊比利亞與高加索阿爾巴尼亞的國王與王子派來人質、承認羅馬宗主，兩地從此納入羅馬的勢力圈。版圖上最直接的結果是科爾基斯的納入：黑海東岸第一次出現羅馬的常駐安排與貢賦關係。戰利品方面，龐培在法西斯與狄俄斯庫里亞斯一帶取得米特里達梯積存的金銀與兵器，數量在古代記載中大得驚人，也是他日後在羅馬權力的資本。但戰役留下的並非一份乾淨的勝利：羅馬沒有在高加索建立行省，只以附庸國、條款與象徵性駐軍維持控制，遠征的直接收入遠小於安全與商路的收益；而高加索的忠誠從來只是客戶式的忠誠，米特里達梯在公元前63年死後，羅馬又在亞美尼亞與安息之間糾纏數十年。從更大的格局看，這場公元前65年的高加索戰役，是羅馬從地中海走向中亞內陸的一次戰略試探：它證明了龐培可以在不必事事報請元老院的情況下自行決定遠征的方式與終點，也為後來龐培與凱撒在東、西兩線對峙時，龐培掌握的亞洲財源與高加索邊界，埋下了伏線。
resultEn: As a campaign the result was a Roman victory: Colchis fell, the last base that Mithridates VI held in the Caucasus was taken from him, and the pretender who fled to the Bosporus was killed by his own men; the kings and princes of Iberia and of Caucasian Albania sent hostages and acknowledged Roman suzerainty, and both countries entered the Roman sphere of influence. The most direct territorial consequence was the incorporation of Colchis, which for the first time put a Roman resident presence and a tribute relationship on the eastern Black Sea coast. In the way of plunder, Pompey seized the gold, silver and weapons that Mithridates had amassed around Phasis and Dioscurias, a quantity the ancient writers describe as astonishing and which became the capital of his power in Rome. What the campaign did not leave behind, however, was a clean victory: Rome built no province in the Caucasus, holding it instead with client kingdoms, clauses and token garrisons, and the direct revenue of the expedition was far smaller than the security and trade it bought; the loyalty of the Caucasus was in any case only that of a client, and after Mithridates died in 63 BC Rome went on tangling with Armenia and Parthia for decades. On the larger map, this Caucasian campaign of 65 BC was a strategic probe from the Mediterranean towards the interior of Central Asia. It showed that Pompey could decide the manner and the destination of a distant campaign without asking the Senate for authorisation at every step, and it laid the groundwork for the Asian revenues and the Caucasian frontier that Pompey would hold when he and Caesar faced each other on the eastern and western fronts.
